summary: As of 3:28 a.m. on Nov. 19 neither the Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch nor the Fairbanks Police daily bulletin had posted anything for the day, and no new criminal case had been opened at the Fairbanks, Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction courthouses since Nov. 18. One arrest from Nov. 18 reached the police bulletin overnight: a criminal trespass arrest on Twelfth Avenue in Fairbanks, which matches a court file opened the same day. A Fairbanks case number opened and closed on Nov. 18 is no longer searchable in the state's public case database, although the court's own weekly filings report still lists it. The court filing counts below are the weekly report's own counts for its window of Nov. 12 to Nov. 18.

entries.title: Criminal trespass arrest: Ahdalah Panikak Williamson
body: Ahdalah Panikak Williamson, 42, was arrested on a charge of criminal trespass in the second degree - entering or remaining unlawfully on premises - a Class B misdemeanor.
Fairbanks Police say the arrest was made at the 500 block of Twelfth Avenue in Fairbanks on Nov. 18 at 7:24 a.m. Police case 26003501.
A court file was opened the same day on a complaint. Case 4FA-26-02304CR; no court date is set. She is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: A Fairbanks criminal case number has dropped out of the state's public case database
body: A criminal case number opened at the Fairbanks courthouse on Nov. 18 and closed the same day, with the court recording that no complaint or citation was filed, returned a full record in the Alaska CourtView public database on the evening of Nov. 18 and returns no record at all on Nov. 19.
The Alaska Court System's own weekly report of criminal charges filed, run at 9:01 p.m. on Nov. 18, still lists the number, with no charge and no degree of offense recorded against it.
No charge was ever filed in the case and nobody was charged. The court has given no explanation for the difference between its two public records.
